title: Hybrid GPU node provisioning module: Karpenter primary with ASG fallback (Terraform)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Deliver a single Terraform module that provisions GPU-backed node capacity in Private (VPC) EKS clusters where Karpenter is the preferred provisioner but an ASG-based node pool is available as a controlled fallback. The module will be opinionated about safe upgrade paths for GPU drivers, provide robust health checks for GPU readiness, and expose knobs for spot/on-demand mix and warm reserve capacity.

Scope:
- Terraform module (registry-style) to create: Karpenter Provisioner config (with instance selector for GPU families), an ASG node pool (mixed instances), IAM roles/policies, launch template with NVIDIA AMI selection, and optional SSM agent bootstrap.
- Upgrade hooks: lifecycle hooks and node-drain automation for driver upgrades coordinated with a GPU-driver DaemonSet rollout (nvidia-device-plugin + driver installer).
- Health checks: Node readiness gating on NVIDIA driver + nvidia-smi check, GPU exporter for Prometheus, custom NodeCondition (redwood/gpu-ready) and automated remediation (cordon/drain + recreate) for degraded nodes.
- Fallback policy: Karpenter preferred; when Karpenter cannot satisfy binpack/instance constraints within X seconds or spot availability drops below threshold, Terraform-configured autoscaling group receives a managed increment. Policy is configurable per-environment.
- Spot handling: graceful cordon on spot-notice, hot-warm pool design (small warm ASG with on-demand capacity), and spot interruption metrics surfaced in Console.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Single module vs two modules: chose single module to simplify customer consumption (module toggles enable/disable features), but split internal tf files to keep complexity manageable.
- Karpenter-first: Karpenter provides better bin-packing and fast provisioning for bursty inference; fallback ASG is more predictable for reserved workloads. This incurs extra infra cost but improves SLA for Dedicated-like use cases in Private.
- Driver upgrades via DaemonSet + node lifecycle hooks: avoids custom AMI rebuilds, shortens upgrade window, but requires robust health checks and cordon/drain orchestration to avoid capacity loss.

Non-goals: handle on-prem kubeadm clusters (out of scope), create custom AMIs for every model variant, integrate with external cluster-autoscaler (we rely on Karpenter + ASG).

Expected deliverables: Terraform module with examples for us-west-2/us-east-1, a README with recommended parameters, Helm values for GPU driver DaemonSet, Terraform tests, CI pipeline job that runs tflint/terratest scenarios, and Prometheus+Grafana dashboard templates for GPUs.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions a Karpenter provisioner and an ASG-based mixed-instance GPU node pool in a VPC EKS cluster using example vars
Karpenter is the primary path: pods that match GPU selectors are scheduled to Karpenter provisioned nodes when capacity exists
When Karpenter cannot fulfill constraints for N seconds (configurable), ASG capacity increases and new nodes join the cluster
GPU-driver upgrade process can be triggered via Terraform variable or annotation and upgrades nodes without losing >= 90% of baseline capacity (canary rollout)
Node healthchecks detect driver mismatch or missing nvidia-smi and automatically cordon/drain + recreate nodes; remediation events appear in the Console dashboard
Prometheus metrics for node_gpu_ready and spot_interruption exported; Grafana dashboard linkable from Console
Examples and docs provided; terratest scenarios validate create/destroy and a simulated spot interruption flow

Build ASG launch template with mixed instances policy and user-data to install SSM + gpu driver bootstrapper
Add IAM roles/policies for node role and instance profile
Implement healthcheck DaemonSet manifest and NodeCondition reporter (uses nvidia-smi + driver version check)
Wire spot interruption hook handler (node-exporter + lambda/SSM runbook) and warm-pool config
Add Terraform variables for fallback thresholds, warm pool size, spot/on-demand split
Add lifecycle hooks & cordon/drain automation to support driver DaemonSet upgrades
Create terratest suites for provisioning, upgrade canary, and spot interruption
Add unit tests (tflint), CI job, and publish initial module to internal registry as private/gpu-provisioner-v1
